comments.body: Seria mejor archivo markdown
Aprovechando que este proyecto arranca de cero, coloquemos nombres de variables y funciones en ingles.

Los scripts `lint`/`lint:fix` usan `eslint .` sin `--ext`, lo que hace que ESLint (v10) no incluya archivos TypeScript (`.ts/.mts/.cts`) al recorrer directorios; esto contradice el objetivo de “soporte completo para TypeScript”.

Al incorporar `eslint@10.9.1`, el árbol de dependencias exige Node `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24`; sin un campo `engines` en `package.json`, es fácil que alguien intente instalar con una versión menor y falle el `npm install`/`npm ci` por incompatibilidad de engines.

`typescript-eslint@8.70.0` declara peerDependency `typescript: ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0"`, pero en `package.json` se permite `typescript: ^6.0.3` (lo que habilita `6.1.x` en adelante). Eso puede romper la instalación o generar warnings cuando se actualicen dependencias.

comments.body: The icon rendering logic is incorrect. The expression `action.icon || ImportedIcons[action.icon?.name]` will always evaluate to `action.icon` because it's already a reference to the icon component. The fallback using `ImportedIcons[action.icon?.name]` will never execute. Since `action.icon` is already the correct component reference, this should simply be `React.createElement(action.icon, { size: 14 })`.

The SVG paths for PeopleFillIcon appear to be incomplete. The second path element has coordinate values starting with negative decimals (e.g., `.93`, `.837`, `-1.58`) which suggests the path data is truncated or corrupted. This should be reviewed against the original Bootstrap Icons implementation to ensure the icon renders correctly.

OfficeRibbon should not be exported from the atoms index file because it doesn't exist in the atoms directory. OfficeRibbon has been moved to the organisms directory. This export will cause an error. The correct export should be from the organisms index file instead.

The SVG path for ShieldIcon appears to be corrupted or truncated. There's a malformed section in the path data (`.72.04 1.41.1.1.94.78 1.04 1.2.38 1.34-.32.03-.1.08-.2.13-.3z`) that contains incomplete coordinate values and appears to be missing proper path commands. This should be reviewed against the original Bootstrap Icons implementation to ensure the icon renders correctly.

The inline IIFE for rendering icons is unnecessarily complex and reduces code readability. Since the icon property already contains the component reference, a simpler approach would be to directly use React.createElement or JSX syntax. Consider refactoring to: `React.createElement(currentContext.primary.icon, { size: 24 })` or creating a separate helper function to render icons.

comments.body: `jest.mock('../repositories/holidayRepository')` is declared after requiring `./holidayService`. Since `holidayService` imports the repository at module load time, this can result in the real repository being captured before the mock is applied (and the tests will fail unless a transform hoists the mock). Move the `jest.mock(...)` call above the `require('./holidayService')` (or require the service after mocking) so the dependency is reliably mocked.

The repository module exports a class instance (`module.exports = new HolidayRepository()`), so Jest's automatic mocking may not generate `create`/etc. as `jest.fn()`s because the methods live on the prototype (not as own properties). This makes `holidayRepository.create.mockResolvedValue(...)` unreliable (likely `create` is undefined). Prefer providing an explicit mock factory for `../repositories/holidayRepository` that defines `create: jest.fn()` (and any other methods used), or switch to `jest.spyOn` on the real module export.

`package-lock.json` is present in the repo, but this PR adds a new devDependency (`jest`) without updating the lockfile. Please regenerate/commit the updated lockfile so installs are deterministic and CI uses the same dependency graph.

The lazy-loaded page declarations are very repetitive and hard to scan/maintain (each route repeats the same `import(...).then(...)` unwrapping pattern). Consider extracting a small helper (e.g., `lazyNamed(path, exportName)`) or grouping per-feature imports to reduce duplication and make future route additions less error-prone.

`client/package.json` sets `"type": "module"`, so this Vite config is executed as ESM and `__dirname` is not defined. As written, `path.resolve(__dirname, './src')` will throw at startup. Use an ESM-safe approach (e.g., derive the directory from `import.meta.url`, or use `new URL('./src', import.meta.url)` with `fileURLToPath`).
